name: sanitize_document
description: Scrub an open session document. By default it removes revision ids, authorship, embedded EXIF and hidden text PII. Tracked changes and comments are kept, with the text of every tracked deletion, unless you ask: acceptAllRevisions:true accepts all tracked changes (deleted text is removed) and stripComments:true removes comments. The CLI presets (bare sanitize, --client-safe, --metadata-only, --redact-pii) turn both on; this tool does not. Macro/active parts are removed on request. It uses the same engine scrub path as CLI sanitize. Body text is kept. Options mirror the engine scrub keys 1:1 (zeroRetention, purgeRSIDs, purgeAuthors, purgeExif, purgePII, acceptAllRevisions, stripComments, replacementAuthor, allowMacros, stripMacros); omitted options take engine defaults. With acceptAllRevisions it returns E_VALIDATION and no file when revision markup remains that cannot be resolved. allowMacros and stripMacros together fail with E_VALIDATION. The PII check looks for email addresses; phone numbers (formatted, or digits after a label such as "phone", "tel", "mobile", "fax", "call" or "contact"); US Social Security numbers (123-45-6789, or 9 digits after "SSN" or "Social Security"); runs of 13 to 19 digits (card numbers). It does not look for other national ID numbers (for example CPF and CNPJ); names; postal addresses; other digit runs without a label. Returns {ok:true,sessionId,revision,dirty,removedRSIDs,purgedAuthors,strippedExifBytes,purgedPII,bodyPII,piiCoverage,acceptedRevisions,strippedComments,strippedMacros,macroParts,filesTouched,droppedRogue,...} plus the standard redoCleared signal when a redo chain is dropped. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","stripMacros":true} -> scrubbed session at a new revision (save after).
